UNREGISGTERED SCHOOL

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A private school education at reasonable price tag is bound to come with a catch – we investigate a school that sells a dream but falls short when it comes to compliance.

Unique Selling Point:
- INVESTIGATION ELEMENT
- CONGRONT


Summary:
Sion Private Academy sells a dream – an affordable private school education for your children. Small classes, exceptional standard of education for a reasonable price tag.

This school has 1200 learners.

What the school doesn’t have is a valid Department of Education registration, accreditation to teach their syllabus and qualified educators.

It’s a winning combination. Parents are angry and the Department of Education is not doing much.



Further information:
This what they don’t have:
1. They don’t have a valid EMIS registration number from the Department of Education – under the Education Act the school should be shut down immediately and people responsible could be jailed.
2. They don’t have 80% of their educations registered with the South African Council for Educators – this is also illegal. Some teachers are not even qualified. And the management staff don’t have the necessary qualifications or experience and some are barely old enough to have finished their studies.
3. They are not accredited by Umalusi to teach CAPS syllabus.

They are still open. They still collect school fees. They still attempt to teach.
There are three campuses.
4. Sion Stepping Stones
5. Sion Private Academy in Boksburg
6. Sion Privat Academy Clearwater Campus

Boksburg is registered with the Department of Education. Not the other two. You cannot recycle EMIS numbers and use them interchangeably. Clear water is the new campus – from the third term which is about to start, the school will operate only from there. It does not have an EMIS registration number.

A group of parents have taken them on, the school has responded with a defamation case and bombarded with cease-and-desist letters – the parents have defended these motions successfully.

We have audio recordings from the school management contradicting itself and out right lying. We have audio recording from the Department of Education confirming the school is operating illegally.

UNDERCOVER ELEMENT
I initially suggested this, but it is school holidays at the moment. We are trying to get in today or tomorrow – but it may be that we don’t get this element.

The premise for our visits is that we go in pretending to want to register a kid – get the school tour and sales pitch.

CONFRONTATIONS
DEPT OF EDUCTION
I’ve asked for an interview with the GP Department of Education. Masa is helping – she knows the spokesperson and MEC. If that doesn’t work by midday – I’ll reach out the National Office. Because the GP Department knows about the discrepancies and have not taken the school to task. Their take is that they should help the school become compliant because as it stands Gauteng is in desperate need of schools. BUT we ask – at who’s expense? The kids!

** Some of the children that have been removed from the school, were assessed at the new schools and actually taken back a grade because their level of education was not at the level needed for the grade they were in at Sion.

THE SCHOOL
I’ve made contact with the owner Ulandi Senekal via whatsapp, I’ve sent and email to the school general email address and then her attorney. They will come back to me. I’m a little nervous that they are going to hide behind the attorneys and that we end up with a written response.


THE INTERVIEWS
1. STUART WILLCOCK – PARENT GROUP REPRESENTATIVE
He represents a group of parents that have uncovered the non-compliance issues. The group has been sued by the school for defamation and a second case was brought against one of the parents in their personal capacity. First case was thrown out without costs. And the second case was thrown out with costs.

Stuart’s kids were in the school, they’ve been removed – he is well spoken and reasonable in his argument.

2. MELANIE POTGIETER – PARENT AND FORMER EMPLOYEE AT SION
Melanie’s kids had to go back a grade in the new school. Melanie worked as a receptionist at the school – she noticed something was up with the registration and accreditation, started asking questions and got a promotion and a raise. But the moolah didn’t materialize, because Sion pays admin staff different amounts based on a “review process”. Melanie resigned. She has the inside track on the unqualified teachers, the turn over of staff and has an understanding of how the school operated. She alerted Stuart and the other parents.

** Her drawback is that she owed school fees – BUT had a payment plan that deducted half her salary every month to cover the debt.

3. DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION

5. RIGHT OF REPLIES TO THE TEACHERS WE’LL NAME

Script:


STRUCTURE: UNREGISTERED SCHOOL

VO: Is there anything more likely to anger responsible parents than their children’s futures being gambled with? Well, that’s precisely how a group of concerned Johannesburg parents are feeling.

LINK: When it comes to education, parents want the best for their kids - private schooling, individual attention and state of the art facilities. And wouldn't it be great if this came at a reasonable price tag?

VO: That’s exactly what Sion Clearwater Campus in Boksburg , claims to offer parents.

STUART: It was just a win win situation. //the school was so amazing, I pulled all my kids //and put them into that school.

VO: In January 2022, Stuart Willcock enrolled his three daughters into the brand new Sion Clearwater Campus - paying about R3500, per child, per month, in school fees .

LINK: I must admit, the school does look pretty impressive, but looking the part doesn't cut it when it comes to education in this country.

VO11: By the end of the first term, Willcock and some of the other parents say the dream they were sold had become a nightmare.

The first red flag was the high turnover of teachers at the school and discrepancies with tests and grading.

STUART: we started questioning like, but are These guys actually qualified to be in these positions? // these teachers are 20, 19 year old, 22 year old.

VO: As a result, some parents believe their children have suffered academically, and they want answers.

STUART: There's no seriousness to any of these questions. Everything is just okay. It's not You are. You are actually busy interfering with my child's education.

VO: We went undercover at Sion Clearwater Campus posing as interested parents . It’s presented as a fully registered modern facility, with a hands-on management team, focused on giving learners personalised attention.

We briefly met one of the school founders - Ulandie Senekal and also the Deputy Principal , Donovan Kemp who explained that Clearwater Campus is one of three schools under the Sion umbrella.

UNDERCOVER
DK - We moved to this premises, beginning of this year – when Clearwater started – but we still had the three schools – Sion Private Academy in Boksburg, Sion Stepping Stones, and then this campus.

LINK: When an independent private school opens, there are a few boxes that need to be ticked in order for it to operate legally. And only once that's done can the school open its doors for business.

VO: The law requires 3 things:
- EACH independent private school needs a dedicated registration number, called an EMIS number, issued by the provincial Department of Education -
- When offering a South African curriculum, the specific school needs accreditation from the education standards body, Umalusi ,
- and teachers must hold teaching qualifications and be registered with the SA/South Africa Council for Educators, or SACE.

CONFIDENCE: The laws of the country are very clear.

VO: Confidence Dikgole is from ISASA, the Independent Schools Association of Southern Africa, the region’s largest… and oldest voluntTRY membership organisation for private schools.

CONFIDENCE: //anyone who stands in front of the children must be registered with SACE and again is for purposes of safeguarding our kids in schools, to make sure that people who are appointed to teach are suitably qualified to teach..

VO: When a group of 10 parents started publicly questioning the Sion Clearwater Campus’ legitimacy, they were slapped with a defamation suit by the school’s owners.

VO: In court documents, the school included a list of staff . Of the forty nine teaching staff on the list - only 7 have full professional SACE registrations, 25 had provisional numbers, while the rest didn’t have a valid registration number .

CONFIDENCE: provisional registration would be granted to somebody who is studying towards a teaching qualification - whether it is a BEd or a post-grad in Education. / they can't be allowed to teach alone in a class

VO: One of the teachers is the owner’s daughter, MEGAN SENEKAL, who matriculated in 2020. Megan admitted to us that she is still studying, yet teaches her own class, under occasional supervision .

MS: I show my lessons to them before, then they do class inspection once I do my lessons, not in every single lesson, but they do sit in while I do a lesson. //
MASA: // So you're teaching unsupervised in the class sometimes, which is what you've just said?
MS: Yes. //
MASA: And there we have it. 20 year old Megan, the daughter of the owners, has just admitted that she teaches kids and she's still studying.

VO: Ms Senekal is not the only teacher that stands out . We met Donovan Kemp during our undercover visit.

DK – The one deputy principal is for the primary school, we have a deputy principal for Grade 7 to Grade 9 and then 10, 11, 12 – is myself.

VO: Kemp is 23 years old. Sion claims he has SEVEN years’ teaching experience - that would mean he qualified and started teaching at the age of 16 .

MASA: Are you also the deputy principal?
DK: No, I'm not. //

VO: That’s odd, apart from him confirming it in our undercover footage , he also signs reports as the Deputy Principal .

MASA: I just wanted to check your teaching qualifications. Do you have them?
DK: Thank you.GOODBYE
MASA: What teaching qualification do you have DOnovan?
BEEP BEEP
MASA: And he's gone. Thank you, goodbye.

VO: But that’s not where the allegations end, the group of the concerned parents uncovered even more questionable details.

STUART: // we started emailing all of the bodies and all the board different bodies
came back to us and advised that they were not registered.

VO: Multiple officials from the Gauteng Department of Education, SACE and accreditation bodies confirmed in writing that Sion Clearwater Campus was not properly registered or accredited at the time .

LINK: From all the correspondence that we've seen, it appears that Sion Clearwater is not compliant, but they insist that they are and all the officials are wrong.

VO: Sion’s owners declined an on-camera interview, responding only in writing.

They state there is only one EMIS registration number and that the Sion Clearwater Campus “did not operate as an individual entity”…claiming “Sion Private Academy is located at, and operating from the Clearwater Campus”.

UPSOUND BUZZER

VO: That’s not exactly true. Listen to this clip sent to parents in May, by the owner Ulandie Senekal, she clarifies the amalgamation of the schools - take note - it’s plural….SCHOOLS - she is referring to more than one school joining up.

ULANDIE: There's multiple reasons for the merger, but I absolutely say that unity of the schools was number one of it.

VO: This amalgamation only happened this week as the third school term started. When Sion Clearwater Campus opened its doors in January, it didn’t meet all the legal requirements .

CONFIDENCE: // No school should be operating unless it is registered by the Department of Education to be on the right side of the law. //

VO: Provincial Education Departments are responsible for regulating both public and private schools - ensuring they play by the rules. Steve Mabona is the Gauteng Spokesperson.

MASA: Your department is aware of this independent school. They are operating without registration from your department. //
STEVE: Well, according to information at our disposal, the school is registered. They even have an EMIS number. M3

VO: An EMIS Registration number is allocated by the Education Department at a specific address, only once it’s checked and vetted the specific school. What Mabona is referring to, is the one allocated to the original Sion Private Academy - NOT Sion Clearwater Campus.

STEVE: They have relocated. // We have one school that relocated from the previous address. Now ther are in a new address. - we have one school we don’t have two shcools
MASA: Steve, there's two schools here. //M11// Why are you covering up for them STEVE: no,no, what we have is the relocated from one school to the other. //35

VO: Mr. Mabona repeated the same line during the interview - but just saying the same thing over and over, doesn’t make it true. There were actually three different schools - open at the same time, using one EMIS registration number.

But, Dikogole has processed these types of applications for ISASA…and says, even if it was just a relocation, it’s not a simple transfer of registration…

CONFIDENCE: As soon as you took a different physical address, that's where then you need to have a different registration with a different number.

MASA: As far as I understand, this EMIS number cannot be transferred. It is attached to a specific location an establishment.
STEVE: No,
MASA: this is where it is. So an EMIS number you saying can be transferred?
STEVE: They’ve Relocated.

VO: When we asked Mabona about the teachers’ qualifications, it appears the Department again had a different version .

STEVE: //The educators are qualified, M26 // teachers there they are registered…. M29
MASA: But they are not. M29
STEVE: according to information at my disposal was that the educators are registered with the SACE and those that would have not been registered probably is your teacher assistants //M30
MASA: //Most of them. If you look at this list from page after page, provisional, provisional, provisional. And it keeps going .

VO: Despite putting the irregularities to Mabona and trying to show him the evidence - he point blank refused to even look at it.

MASA: I put it to you, Steve, that the information at your disposal is incorrect. //
STEVE: No, no, no. We we can confirm that we have a school that is relocated and we welcome to support them because they are a good school.// M14 // There's nothing wrong here with this school.

VO: But denials that rules are being bent don’t benefit the learners.

STUART: we're also fighting against the system. // if we're going to have quality education in South Africa, then surely parents should // start standing against the system that is allowing this in this country.

END




PROMOS
PROMO 1 - 21 seconds
VO: When schools aren’t legally compliant - they shouldn’t be operating. But these rules don’t seem to apply to one Gauteng school.

STUART: // we started emailing all of the bodies and all the board different bodies
came back to us and advised that they were not registered. M9

VO: IS IT A COMPLETE DISREGARD FOR THE LAW OR A COVER UP?
PROMO 2 - 21 seconds
VO: PArents were sold a dream - private schooling education at a reasonable price.

BUT did the school tick all the boxes with registration, accreditation and qualified teachers - some parents are not convinced.

STUART: It's not okay. // You are actually busy interfering with my child's education. M12

PROMO 3 - 11 seconds
VO: A private school education at reasonable price is bound to come with a catch – we investigate a school that sells a dream… but allegedly falls short on compliance… and might jeopardise learners academically.

The first red flag was the high turnover of teachers at the school and discrepancies with tests and grading. STUART: we started questioning like, but are These guys actually qualified to be in these positions? // these teachers are 20, 19 year old, 22 year old. VO: As a result, some parents believe their children have suffered academically, and they want answers. STUART: There's no seriousness to any of these questions. Everything is just okay. It's not You are. You are actually busy interfering with my child's education. VO: We went undercover at Sion Clearwater Campus posing as interested parents . It’s presented as a fully registered modern facility, with a hands-on management team, focused on giving learners personalised attention. We briefly met one of the school founders - Ulandie Senekal and also the Deputy Principal , Donovan Kemp who explained that Clearwater Campus is one of three schools under the Sion umbrella. UNDERCOVER DK - We moved to this premises, beginning of this year – when Clearwater started – but we still had the three schools – Sion Private Academy in Boksburg, Sion Stepping Stones, and then this campus. LINK: When an independent private school opens, there are a few boxes that need to be ticked in order for it to operate legally. And only once that's done can the school open its doors for business. VO: The law requires 3 things: - EACH independent private school needs a dedicated registration number, called an EMIS number, issued by the provincial Department of Education - - When offering a South African curriculum, the specific school needs accreditation from the education standards body, Umalusi , - and teachers must hold teaching qualifications and be registered with the SA/South Africa Council for Educators, or SACE. CONFIDENCE: The laws of the country are very clear. VO: Confidence Dikgole is from ISASA, the Independent Schools Association of Southern Africa, the region’s largest… and oldest voluntTRY membership organisation for private schools. CONFIDENCE: //anyone who stands in front of the children must be registered with SACE and again is for purposes of safeguarding our kids in schools, to make sure that people who are appointed to teach are suitably qualified to teach.. VO: When a group of 10 parents started publicly questioning the Sion Clearwater Campus’ legitimacy, they were slapped with a defamation suit by the school’s owners. VO: In court documents, the school included a list of staff . Of the forty nine teaching staff on the list - only 7 have full professional SACE registrations, 25 had provisional numbers, while the rest didn’t have a valid registration number . CONFIDENCE: provisional registration would be granted to somebody who is studying towards a teaching qualification - whether it is a BEd or a post-grad in Education. / they can't be allowed to teach alone in a class VO: One of the teachers is the owner’s daughter, MEGAN SENEKAL, who matriculated in 2020. Megan admitted to us that she is still studying, yet teaches her own class, under occasional supervision . MS: I show my lessons to them before, then they do class inspection once I do my lessons, not in every single lesson, but they do sit in while I do a lesson. // MASA: // So you're teaching unsupervised in the class sometimes, which is what you've just said? MS: Yes. // MASA: And there we have it. 20 year old Megan, the daughter of the owners, has just admitted that she teaches kids and she's still studying. VO: Ms Senekal is not the only teacher that stands out . We met Donovan Kemp during our undercover visit. DK – The one deputy principal is for the primary school, we have a deputy principal for Grade 7 to Grade 9 and then 10, 11, 12 – is myself. VO: Kemp is 23 years old. Sion claims he has SEVEN years’ teaching experience - that would mean he qualified and started teaching at the age of 16 . MASA: Are you also the deputy principal? DK: No, I'm not. // VO: That’s odd, apart from him confirming it in our undercover footage , he also signs reports as the Deputy Principal . MASA: I just wanted to check your teaching qualifications. Do you have them? DK: Thank you.GOODBYE MASA: What teaching qualification do you have DOnovan? BEEP BEEP MASA: And he's gone. Thank you, goodbye. VO: But that’s not where the allegations end, the group of the concerned parents uncovered even more questionable details. STUART: // we started emailing all of the bodies and all the board different bodies came back to us and advised that they were not registered. VO: Multiple officials from the Gauteng Department of Education, SACE and accreditation bodies confirmed in writing that Sion Clearwater Campus was not properly registered or accredited at the time . LINK: From all the correspondence that we've seen, it appears that Sion Clearwater is not compliant, but they insist that they are and all the officials are wrong. VO: Sion’s owners declined an on-camera interview, responding only in writing. They state there is only one EMIS registration number and that the Sion Clearwater Campus “did not operate as an individual entity”…claiming “Sion Private Academy is located at, and operating from the Clearwater Campus”. UPSOUND BUZZER VO: That’s not exactly true. Listen to this clip sent to parents in May, by the owner Ulandie Senekal, she clarifies the amalgamation of the schools - take note - it’s plural….SCHOOLS - she is referring to more than one school joining up. ULANDIE: There's multiple reasons for the merger, but I absolutely say that unity of the schools was number one of it. VO: This amalgamation only happened this week as the third school term started. When Sion Clearwater Campus opened its doors in January, it didn’t meet all the legal requirements . CONFIDENCE: // No school should be operating unless it is registered by the Department of Education to be on the right side of the law. // VO: Provincial Education Departments are responsible for regulating both public and private schools - ensuring they play by the rules. Steve Mabona is the Gauteng Spokesperson. MASA: Your department is aware of this independent school. They are operating without registration from your department. // STEVE: Well, according to information at our disposal, the school is registered. They even have an EMIS number. M3 VO: An EMIS Registration number is allocated by the Education Department at a specific address, only once it’s checked and vetted the specific school. What Mabona is referring to, is the one allocated to the original Sion Private Academy - NOT Sion Clearwater Campus. STEVE: They have relocated. // We have one school that relocated from the previous address. Now ther are in a new address. - we have one school we don’t have two shcools MASA: Steve, there's two schools here. //M11// Why are you covering up for them STEVE: no,no, what we have is the relocated from one school to the other. //35 VO: Mr. Mabona repeated the same line during the interview - but just saying the same thing over and over, doesn’t make it true. There were actually three different schools - open at the same time, using one EMIS registration number. But, Dikogole has processed these types of applications for ISASA…and says, even if it was just a relocation, it’s not a simple transfer of registration… CONFIDENCE: As soon as you took a different physical address, that's where then you need to have a different registration with a different number. MASA: As far as I understand, this EMIS number cannot be transferred. It is attached to a specific location an establishment. STEVE: No, MASA: this is where it is. So an EMIS number you saying can be transferred? STEVE: They’ve Relocated. VO: When we asked Mabona about the teachers’ qualifications, it appears the Department again had a different version . STEVE: //The educators are qualified, M26 // teachers there they are registered…. M29 MASA: But they are not. M29 STEVE: according to information at my disposal was that the educators are registered with the SACE and those that would have not been registered probably is your teacher assistants //M30 MASA: //Most of them. If you look at this list from page after page, provisional, provisional, provisional. And it keeps going . VO: Despite putting the irregularities to Mabona and trying to show him the evidence - he point blank refused to even look at it. MASA: I put it to you, Steve, that the information at your disposal is incorrect. // STEVE: No, no, no. We we can confirm that we have a school that is relocated and we welcome to support them because they are a good school.// M14 // There's nothing wrong here with this school. VO: But denials that rules are being bent don’t benefit the learners. STUART: we're also fighting against the system. // if we're going to have quality education in South Africa, then surely parents should // start standing against the system that is allowing this in this country. END PROMOS PROMO 1 - 21 seconds VO: When schools aren’t legally compliant - they shouldn’t be operating. But these rules don’t seem to apply to one Gauteng school. STUART: // we started emailing all of the bodies and all the board different bodies came back to us and advised that they were not registered. M9 VO: IS IT A COMPLETE DISREGARD FOR THE LAW OR A COVER UP? PROMO 2 - 21 seconds VO: PArents were sold a dream - private schooling education at a reasonable price. BUT did the school tick all the boxes with registration, accreditation and qualified teachers - some parents are not convinced. STUART: It's not okay. // You are actually busy interfering with my child's education. M12 PROMO 3 - 11 seconds VO: A private school education at reasonable price is bound to come with a catch – we investigate a school that sells a dream… but allegedly falls short on compliance… and might jeopardise learners academically.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A private school education at reasonable price tag is bound to come with a catch – we investigate a school that sells a dream but falls short when it comes to compliance.
metadata.Summary: Sion Private Academy sells a dream – an affordable private school education for your children. Small classes, exceptional standard of education for a reasonable price tag. This school has 1200 learners. What the school doesn’t have is a valid Department of Education registration, accreditation to teach their syllabus and qualified educators. It’s a winning combination. Parents are angry and the Department of Education is not doing much.
metadata.Further information: This what they don’t have: 1. They don’t have a valid EMIS registration number from the Department of Education – under the Education Act the school should be shut down immediately and people responsible could be jailed. 2. They don’t have 80% of their educations registered with the South African Council for Educators – this is also illegal. Some teachers are not even qualified. And the management staff don’t have the necessary qualifications or experience and some are barely old enough to have finished their studies. 3. They are not accredited by Umalusi to teach CAPS syllabus. They are still open. They still collect school fees. They still attempt to teach. There are three campuses. 4. Sion Stepping Stones 5. Sion Private Academy in Boksburg 6. Sion Privat Academy Clearwater Campus Boksburg is registered with the Department of Education. Not the other two. You cannot recycle EMIS numbers and use them interchangeably. Clear water is the new campus – from the third term which is about to start, the school will operate only from there. It does not have an EMIS registration number. A group of parents have taken them on, the school has responded with a defamation case and bombarded with cease-and-desist letters – the parents have defended these motions successfully. We have audio recordings from the school management contradicting itself and out right lying. We have audio recording from the Department of Education confirming the school is operating illegally. UNDERCOVER ELEMENT I initially suggested this, but it is school holidays at the moment. We are trying to get in today or tomorrow – but it may be that we don’t get this element. The premise for our visits is that we go in pretending to want to register a kid – get the school tour and sales pitch. CONFRONTATIONS DEPT OF EDUCTION I’ve asked for an interview with the GP Department of Education. Masa is helping – she knows the spokesperson and MEC. If that doesn’t work by midday – I’ll reach out the National Office. Because the GP Department knows about the discrepancies and have not taken the school to task. Their take is that they should help the school become compliant because as it stands Gauteng is in desperate need of schools. BUT we ask – at who’s expense? The kids! ** Some of the children that have been removed from the school, were assessed at the new schools and actually taken back a grade because their level of education was not at the level needed for the grade they were in at Sion. THE SCHOOL I’ve made contact with the owner Ulandi Senekal via whatsapp, I’ve sent and email to the school general email address and then her attorney. They will come back to me. I’m a little nervous that they are going to hide behind the attorneys and that we end up with a written response. THE INTERVIEWS 1. STUART WILLCOCK – PARENT GROUP REPRESENTATIVE He represents a group of parents that have uncovered the non-compliance issues. The group has been sued by the school for defamation and a second case was brought against one of the parents in their personal capacity. First case was thrown out without costs. And the second case was thrown out with costs. Stuart’s kids were in the school, they’ve been removed – he is well spoken and reasonable in his argument. 2. MELANIE POTGIETER – PARENT AND FORMER EMPLOYEE AT SION Melanie’s kids had to go back a grade in the new school. Melanie worked as a receptionist at the school – she noticed something was up with the registration and accreditation, started asking questions and got a promotion and a raise. But the moolah didn’t materialize, because Sion pays admin staff different amounts based on a “review process”. Melanie resigned. She has the inside track on the unqualified teachers, the turn over of staff and has an understanding of how the school operated. She alerted Stuart and the other parents. ** Her drawback is that she owed school fees – BUT had a payment plan that deducted half her salary every month to cover the debt. 3.
